content.text:
What kind of story is Anne of Green Gables?

Anne of Green Gables is a coming-of-age story about Anne, an adopted orphan girl who brightens everyone around her with her rich imagination and cheerful positivity. Her pluckiness in getting back up even after making mistakes gives children great strength.

The original story of Anne of Green Gables

The original is "Anne of Green Gables," published in 1908 by Canadian author Lucy Maud Montgomery. Set on Prince Edward Island in Canada, it's a warm story of the adopted Anne becoming family with the siblings Marilla and Matthew and growing up.

content.alt: Anne of Green Gables - Anne of Green Gables plot summary
content.text:
Anne of Green Gables plot summary

Adopted by mistake in place of a boy, Anne is awkward at first, but with her rich imagination, honesty, and warm heart she wins the love of her family and the townspeople. Even through mistakes big and small, she always stays positive, gets back up, and grows up wonderfully.

content.alt: Anne of Green Gables - The lessons of Anne of Green Gables
content.text:
The lessons of Anne of Green Gables

The core message is the power of a rich imagination and positivity, and the courage to get back up even after making mistakes. Try building a habit with your child of looking back on the day positively, with a question like, "What was a good thing that happened today?"
content.caption: The positivity to rise again

content.alt: Anne of Green Gables - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Read Anne's rich imaginative lines with excitement and vividness. Spark imagination with a question like, "How would Anne give this a wonderful name?" and, in the scenes with mistakes, follow up with positivity: "It's okay, you can try again." Suitable for ages 5-7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Anne of Green Gables good for?
A. It's suitable for ages 5-7. With its themes of imagination and positivity, it's good for a time when a sense of self is growing.

Q. Is it the same as "Anne of Green Gables" the novel?
A. Yes, it's the same work; it's simply called by different titles.

Q. What kind of conversation is good to have?
A. Try talking together about "finding the good in things," "trying again after a mistake," and "enjoying life through imagination."

Classic fairy tales to read together

If you enjoyed this story, try reading these classic fairy tales too.
